reason: Combined exfoliation from a retinoid and a BHA raises the risk of barrier damage, redness and peeling.
handling: Separate across the day (one AM, one PM) or alternate nights; never layer in the same routine step.
source: American Academy of Dermatology — 'Retinoid do's and don'ts' (aad.org/retinoids)

reason: Benzoyl peroxide can oxidise and deactivate retinol when applied together, reducing the effect of both.
handling: Use on alternate evenings rather than the same routine step.
source: Kircik LH, 'The role of benzoyl peroxide in the new treatment paradigm for acne', J Drugs Dermatol (2016)

reason: Benzoyl peroxide oxidises vitamin C, reducing its antioxidant stability and effectiveness.
handling: Vitamin C in the morning, benzoyl peroxide in the evening.
source: Del Rosso JQ et al., 'Status Report on Topical Benzoyl Peroxide', J Clin Aesthet Dermatol (2020)

reason: Both are low-pH actives; stacking them in one step can increase irritation on sensitive skin, though many tolerate it fine.
handling: Space them across the day if stinging or redness occurs; otherwise no hard restriction.
source: Draelos ZD, 'Cosmetic Dermatology: Products and Procedures', 2nd ed. (2015), ch. on combining actives
